coach.verdict: Recovery week: both A sessions done, but Tuesday's run turned into the week's hard session.
points: Long run (Thu): 8.5 km in 50 min at 5:53/km, HR 137, max 150. Easy, as written.
Long ride (Sun, Zwift): about 1:50 by the watch at HR 143 vs 2 hrs at 145-165 W. Zwift logged only 52 min moving (149 W average), so power is partial.
Tuesday run in place of the bike: 7.1 km at 4:54/km, HR 160, last 2 km at HR 176-181. Wednesday sweet spot done, shortened (43 min moving).
Friday 82 min HIIT and Saturday tennis on top: extra load in a recovery week.
Recovery fine overall (HRV 7-day 93 vs baseline 89, resting HR 45 vs 47), but Saturday night was 5.8 h sleep and HRV 26 (readiness 1), which shows in Sunday's HR 143 at about 150 W.
coach.focus: Week 4 builds again: Thursday 70 min with the Shorter session, Saturday 2.5 hrs Zone 2. Tuesday track controlled, not a race.
flags: Friday HIIT in a recovery week

coach_history.verdict: Bike quality done, but both key sessions came up short of plan.
points: Long run: 9.0 km in 46 min at 5:02/km, HR 143, vs 60 min with 2 x 10 min tempo. No tempo blocks; the whole run sat at a steady 4:46-5:12/km instead.
Thursday bike: 31 min at 198 W with steps to 265 W (114% FTP) and HR to 180, vs 3 x 10 min at 205-215 W. Shorter and harder than written.
Long ride moved to Sunday: 53 km, 2:07 moving, HR 143 vs 2-2.5 hrs. Power meter didn't record, so no watts.
Volume about 4.1 h (bike 3.4 h, run 0.75 h), up from about 2.8 h in week 1.
Recovery markers good: HRV 7-day 93 vs baseline 88, resting HR 46.7 vs 46.6, sleep 6.9 h average with one very short night.
coach_history.focus: Ride and run the sessions as written: sweet spot at 205-215 W, easy at 5:20-5:45/km.

coach_history.verdict: Solid first week: FTP set, steady volume, but sleep is the limiter.
points: FTP test: 245 W for 20 minutes, giving an FTP of 232 W. Pacing was dead even (best 10, 15 and 20 min all 245–246 W) and you finished with a little left.
Cadence averaged about 68 rpm in the test. Aim for 80–90 rpm in bike sessions; most riders hold power better there.
Thursday's 10.3 km at 5:25/km: heart rate rose about 10 bpm at the same pace in the second half. On 4.9 hours' sleep that's expected, but easy runs should stay under about 145 bpm.
Sleep averaged 6.1 hours, with three nights under 5. Overnight HRV is 14% below your 4-week baseline. Sleep is the cheapest performance gain available right now.
coach_history.focus: Get at least 7 hours on the nights before Thursday and Saturday.
